title.narrative: Aimags and Soums Green Regional Development Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative: The program represents a fundamental paradigm shift in applying a transformative model to promote green territorial development and urban-rural linkages, whereby livable human settlements - aimag (province) and soum (subunit of an aimag) centers - become anchors of green agribusinesses that promote sustainable, resilient, and high-carbon sequestration rangeland management. Initially focusing on Mongolia's western aimags, the program will promote climate finance and private sector investment mechanisms that can be replicated countrywide.

Output: Climate-resilient, high-carbon sequestration, and sustainable rangeland and agricultural management implemented Indicator: 90 PUGs and herder groups signed (by both spouses) the updated RUA and sustainable and inclusive pasture management plan and benefited from CPP activities, with 45% female participation Progress/Status: As of 2021, 378 pasture user groups (PUGs) have been registered in the three target aimags under the Green Gold project. Although these PUGs have become inactive after the project ended, 51% of all herders in 34 soums of the Western three aimags have information about pasture use, which can help them reactivate and continue pasture-oriented activities.
Under this performance indicator, implementation of 2 sub-activities is planned for the period 2025-2029. As of 31 December 2025, the progress stands at 11.76%. Amendments to the implementation plan are required.
Breakdown of Completed Work: - Improve Pasture management and Pastureland rehabilitation - 59.0% - Implement Community-Based Investment Projects (CBIPs): 34 Soums - 10.0%
Research activities were conducted in 2025, representing 15% of the activities planned for implementation during 2025-2029.
During fieldwork in the project's target soums of Khovd, Bayan-Ölgii, and Uvs aimags, the current organizational arrangements of pasture user groups and cooperatives, pasture use practices, livestock numbers, and their alignment with pasture carrying capacity were reviewed. The implementation status of internal regulations and agreements was also assessed, and key issues requiring attention to meet relevant standards were identified. Common challenges observed included weaknesses in rotational grazing, seasonal migration practices, appropriate livestock number ratios, collective decision-making, as well as record-keeping and reporting systems. As a result of this work, it was determined that the “Responsible Nomad” standard should be used as the core pasture management tool of the project. Furthermore, the groundwork has been laid for the phased implementation of a certification mechanism aligned with pasture use agreements, pasture management plans, and community-based investment projects. It was also defined as a policy direction to include pasture user groups and cooperatives that meet the standard within the project. During work in the project's 16 target soums, awareness-raising talks and presentations were delivered to approximately 350 herders, representatives of more than 70 cooperatives, and around 150 specialists at the aimag and soum levels on the topics of “Community-Based Investment Project Concepts,” “The Importance of Small-Scale Projects,” and “Cooperative-Based Collective Investment.” Potential investment areas to be implemented under the project—such as pasture protection, water supply, feed production, animal health, and shared equipment—were also introduced. In order to study methodologies, criteria, and implementation practices for community-based projects, meetings were organized with representatives of more than 20 national and international organizations, projects, and cooperatives, facilitating experience sharing. Given that the practical design and implementation of community-based small projects require careful coordination in terms of procurement and financing, this activity was incorporated into the scope of responsibilities of the PIO1 package consultant. Data Source: Aimag and soum governments' monitoring data on land management, and ALAMGAC RUA registration data system Actual value:

Within the framework of the project, it was concluded that support to pasture user groups and cooperatives should be implemented in a phased manner and linked to effective pasture management, livestock number regulation, and cooperative performance, rather than focusing solely on the provision of equipment. Accordingly, it is planned to align equipment and employment support with compliance with the “Responsible Nomad” standard, pasture use agreements, and the implementation of pasture management plans, and to provide such support through community-based investment projects. As a result of the meetings and discussions held, it was further identified that agro-business development plans should be designed not merely to increase production volumes, but to be based on an integrated value chain approach linking cooperatives, secondary cooperatives, processing enterprises, and markets. Data Source: Aimag and soum governments' reports, and MOFALI annual reports on cooperatives Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Target year: 2028 Target value: Y

Output: Climate-resilient, high-carbon sequestration, and sustainable rangeland and agricultural management implemented Indicator: 5 disease-free establishments, 3 aimag-, and 2 inter-soum level veterinary laboratories built Progress/Status: The proposed land for Disease-Free Establishments (Agro-parks) in Deluun soum, Bayan-Ulgii Aimag, and Umnugovi soum, Uvs Aimag, was found unsuitable due to its proximity to industrial areas, oil depots, a landfill, and ger districts. Following on-site inspections with local land, agriculture, and veterinary officials, it was mutually agreed that these locations were inappropriate. Consequently, new, healthier sites away from human and animal traffic, and closer to feed sources, have been selected and are awaiting formal approval by the Citizens' Representatives' Khural.
Under this performance indicator, implementation of 3 sub-activities is planned for the period 2025-2029. As of 31 December 2025, the progress stands at 6.64%.
Breakdown of Completed Work: - Construction of Animal Disease-Free Zone (or Compartment) Facilities: Ölgii, Delgüü, Khovd Aimag - 9.0% - Construction of Quarantine Facilities: Ulaangom, Ömnögovi Soums - 9.0% - Assessment of conditions and needs by province - 100%
Site visits were conducted to the initially proposed locations for establishing Agroparks in the centers of Khovd, Uvs, and Bayan-Ölgii aimags, as well as Deluun soum in Bayan-Ölgii and Ömnögovi soum in Uvs, in coordination with aimag and soum-level Land Offices, Food and Agriculture Departments, Veterinary Services, and local authorities. During the evaluation, some sites were found to be unsuitable for meeting the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) biosafety requirements due to proximity to industrial zones, oil depots, landfills, cement plants, and ger districts. A subsequent survey of suitable sites was conducted, including on-site inspections with aimag authorities. The selected locations were urgently reviewed and endorsed by the Aimag and Soum Citizens' Representative Hural (CRH) to include them in land-use planning documents.
Data Source: Aimag and soum governments' reports on livestock and rural development, and Mongolia State Special Inspection monitoring report Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Target year: 2028 Target value: Y

Output: Climate-resilient, high-carbon sequestration, and sustainable rangeland and agricultural management implemented Indicator: Primary works for the irrigated perimeter of a 1,400-ha fodder and crop farms built, including ecosystem-based water harvesting and conservancy solutions Progress/Status: During visits to Bayan-Ulgii, Uvs, and Khovd aimags, a thorough presentation was given on the legal framework for irrigation systems, specifically addressing requirements for local ownership of headworks and main canals, land use, and water user associations. Additionally, effective strategies for operating shared technical centers, either through cooperatives or with local government support, were proposed. The team also visited several irrigation systems, including "Temee Khuzu" in Deluun soum and "Mandakhyn Am" in Buyant soum (Bayan-Ulgii Aimag), "Khar Khag" in Umnugovi soum, "Khar Tolgoi" in Tarialan soum, and "Baruunturuun" in Baruunturuun soum (Uvs Aimag), and "Khoit Gol" in Darvi soum, and "Tavan Boolt" in Erdeneburen soum (Khovd Aimag).
Under this performance indicator, implementation of 4 sub-activities is planned for the period 2025-2029.
As of 31 December 2025, the progress stands at 6.66%.

Research activities were conducted in 2025, representing 10% of the activities planned for implementation during 2025-2029.
The current status of irrigation systems in the target soums, as well as a list of 52 irrigation systems that could be rehabilitated or newly selected, including their ownership and management by enterprises, was collected, verified, and consolidated from the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry's internal data and local sources, and submitted to the ADB project officer in charge. Baseline surveys on feed cultivation and irrigation systems were collected and consolidated from the target aimags and soums. This baseline study focuses on the location of irrigation systems, water sources, land ownership and tenure, current usage, and the potential for rehabilitation or new construction. It will serve as the foundational basis for future design and investment decision-making.
